newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL tin slips on poor European demand.
newsitem.headline: KL tin slips on poor European demand.

text.p: Malaysian tin price slipped six cents to end at 13.86 ringgit ($5.51) a kg, reversing the last few days' trend, due to a lack of European demand despite further gains in London, traders said.
"KLTM prices slipped today because of poor European buying," a trader said, adding that a smaller premium over the London price also failed to attract strong buying.
"Buyers prefer to watch closely the performance of the London market before taking positions," the trader said.
Scattered buying interest from Europe, Japan and Malaysia was seen.
Traders reported an opening bid of 27 tonnes against offer of 62 tonnes. Turnover was 52 tonnes against 80 on Thursday.
"If the local premium falls further, then more buying will enter the KL market," the trader added. Malaysia's premium over London dropped to $55 a tonne from $100 on Thursday.
Traders remained optimistic that the price would rebound back to the psychological level of 14 ringgit.
